newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: World jute output seen lowed in 1995/96 -IJO.
newsitem.headline: World jute output seen lowed in 1995/96 -IJO.

text.p: The International Jute Organisation (IJO) said on Tuesday world jute production was expected to drop by 13 percent to 2.618 million tonnes in 1995/96 (July-June) but forecast a higher production in 1996/97.

The production of jute fibre, extracted from a reed-like plant, is likely to fall by 27 percent to 674,500 tonnes in Bangladesh, a major exporting country, due to drought and floods, it said in a report.
India, the top of the five producing countries, may have five percent less yield at 1.44 million tonnes this year because of damage caused by drought, the report said.

Jute production in China was expected to fall by 28.9 percent at 270,000 tonnes and output in Thailand was seen to be 4.5 percent lower at 124,000 tonnes while output in Nepal would remain more or less unchanged at around 14,000 tonnes, IJO said.

It said the total land area under jute cultivation in the five major countries decreased to 4.3 million acres (1.74 million hectares) in 1995/96 from 4.6 million acres (1.86 million hectares) in the previous year.
The IJO said jute production in Bangladesh and India might rise to 832,628 tonnes and 1.68 million tonnes respectively in 1996/97.

Bangladesh's export of raw jute was estimated at 231,000 tonnes in 1995/96 against an annual target of 266,000 tonnes. There was no export from India. Pakistan remained the top importer of raw jute followed by European Community countries, the report said.
It said the average export price of raw jute rose to $436 per tonne during January-June compared with $400 in July-December of fiscal 1995/96.

Meanwhile, Rome-based Food and Agriculture Orgainisation (FAO) said that the high raw jute prices and good weather conditions at the time of sowing could result in a sharp rise in area planted in major producing countries this year.
"If weather conditions remain favourable substantially larger crops could be harvested in 1996/97," FAO said in a report.
"Over the medium term, prices of jute fibre and products may come under some downward pressure," it said.
